title: Bisimplicial division and the two Reedy model structures
statement:
Use simplicial sets and standard simplices of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], the Kan and Joyal model structures of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and Reedy model categories of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], in fixed universes. For simplicial sets $U,V$ define $(U\boxtimes V)_{p,q}=U_p\times V_q$. For a bisimplicial set $X$ define simplicial sets
$$(U\backslash X)_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(U\boxtimes\Delta^q,X),\qquad (X/V)_p=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(\Delta^p\boxtimes V,X).$$
For $a:U\to U'$, $b:V\to V'$ and $f:X\to Y$ define
$$\langle a\backslash f\rangle:U'\backslash X\longrightarrow(U'\backslash Y)\times_{U\backslash Y}(U\backslash X),\qquad
\langle f/b\rangle:X/V'\longrightarrow(Y/V')\times_{Y/V}(X/V).$$
For $f:X\to *$ abbreviate these maps by $a\backslash X$ and $X/b$. Write $a\boxtimes' b$ for the map $(U'\boxtimes V)\amalg_{U\boxtimes V}(U\boxtimes V')\to U'\boxtimes V'$. There are natural bijections of lifting problems and their fillers giving
$$(a\boxtimes' b)\pitchfork f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\pitchfork\langle f/b\rangle\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b\pitchfork\langle a\backslash f\rangle,$$
where $i\pitchfork p$ means that every commutative square with left arrow $i$ and right arrow $p$ has a diagonal filler.

The vertical Reedy model structure on bisimplicial sets has monomorphisms as cofibrations, columnwise weak homotopy equivalences as weak equivalences, and fibrations characterized by $\langle\delta_p\backslash f\rangle$ being Kan fibrations for every $p\geq0$, where $\delta_p:\partial\Delta^p\hookrightarrow\Delta^p$ and $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. It is simplicial for the enrichment $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X,Y)_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X\times(*\boxtimes\Delta^q),Y)$. A map $f$ is a vertical Reedy fibration if and only if $\langle a\backslash f\rangle$ is a Kan fibration for every monomorphism $a$; equivalently, $\langle f/b\rangle$ has the right lifting property against all monomorphisms of simplicial sets for every Kan trivial cofibration $b$.

The horizontal Reedy model structure on bisimplicial sets has monomorphisms as cofibrations, rowwise Joyal weak equivalences as weak equivalences, and fibrations characterized by $\langle f/\delta_q\rangle$ being Joyal fibrations for every $q\geq0$. In both these model structures all objects are cofibrant and the factorizations are functorial.

proof.text: All products, pushouts and limits below are formed degreewise in sets, with the induced commuting operators, as follows directly from the functor definition in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Use $\Delta^q_r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([r],[q])$, the representable standard simplex explicitly defined in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Define the operators on $U\backslash X$ and $X/V$ by precomposition with the corresponding standard-simplex maps. To establish the adjunctions explicitly, a map $g:U\boxtimes V\to X$ sends $v\in V_q$ to the map $U\boxtimes\Delta^q\to X$ whose $(p,r)$ component sends $(u,\alpha:[r]\to[q])$ to $g_{p,r}(u,V(\alpha)v)$. Conversely, a simplicial map $h:V\to U\backslash X$ gives $g_{p,q}(u,v)=h_q(v)_{p,q}(u,1_{[q]})$. Naturality of $h$ makes these formulas inverse and makes $g$ natural in both degrees. For the other adjunction, send $u\in U_p$ to the map $\Delta^p\boxtimes V\to X$ whose $(r,q)$ component is $(\alpha:[r]\to[p],v)\mapsto g_{r,q}(U(\alpha)u,v)$. Conversely $k:U\to X/V$ gives $g_{p,q}(u,v)=k_p(u)_{p,q}(1_{[p]},v)$; naturality of $k$ proves that these formulas are inverse. Each formula commutes with precomposition in $U,V$ and postcomposition in $X$. In particular, evaluation on the identity simplex identifies $\Delta^p\backslash X$ with the column $X_{p,\bullet}$, and $X/\Delta^q$ with the row $X_{\bullet,q}$.

source.place: Section 2, definitions preceding Proposition 2.1; explicit degreewise adjunction formulas.

proof.text: Unpack a square from $a\boxtimes' b$ to $f$. Its upper map is exactly a pair of maps $U'\boxtimes V\to X$ and $U\boxtimes V'\to X$ agreeing on $U\boxtimes V$; its lower map is $U'\boxtimes V'\to Y$, and its square equation gives the two required compatibilities with $f$. Under the adjunctions of step 1, these data are exactly a square from $b$ to $\langle a\backslash f\rangle$, and also exactly a square from $a$ to $\langle f/b\rangle$: the agreement is the equation required to map into the indicated pullback. A filler in each description is the same map $U'\boxtimes V'\to X$ restricting to both upper maps and mapping to the lower map. The inverse formulas in step 1 preserve these equations, so they give bijections of squares and of their filler sets, natural in all three arrows. Taking $Y=*$ gives the stated abbreviations, since there is one map from every bisimplicial set to $*$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1; the pushout and pullback equations give the lifting correspondence directly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] to the small category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the Kan model category of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and, in the exchanged ordering of the two directions, the Joyal model category of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Both ground cofibration classes are monomorphisms. In each fixed inner degree, [lem-coef-simplicial-latching-degenerate-subset] identifies the outer latching map with the inclusion of the degenerate subset. Its naturality makes these identifications commute with every inner operator. For a monomorphism $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$, identify $X$ with its image. If $z\in X_{n,q}$ has $z=Y(\sigma)y$ for a proper surjection $\sigma$, choose an increasing section $t$ of $\sigma$. Then $y=Y(t)z$ lies in $X$, so $X_{n,q}\cap D_nY_{\bullet,q}=D_nX_{\bullet,q}$. Consequently the relative latching map is the inclusion $X_{n,q}\cup D_nY_{\bullet,q}\hookrightarrow Y_{n,q}$ in every inner degree. It is a ground cofibration, so $i$ is Reedy cofibrant by the relative latching criterion. Conversely every Reedy cofibration is objectwise a ground cofibration by the Reedy node, hence a monomorphism. This proves the asserted cofibration classes in both orderings. At $n=0$ the new lemma gives the empty latching object, so the same argument includes degree zero.

source.place: Theorem 2.6 and Proposition 2.10, identification of cofibrations; latching calculation expanded using Stacks Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets).

proof.text: By the division adjunction of step 1, $(\partial\Delta^p\backslash X)_q$ is naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^p,X_{\bullet,q})$. Apply [lem-coef-boundary-proper-face-limit] to $T=X_{\bullet,q}$: its naturality in $T$ assembles these sets into the outer matching object $M_pX$, and its restriction clause identifies the matching map with boundary restriction. Thus the relative matching map of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] is $\langle\delta_p\backslash f\rangle$. Objectwise weak equivalences are columnwise weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], giving the vertical model. In the other ordering, step 1 identifies $(X/\partial\Delta^q)_p$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^q,X_{p,\bullet})$. The new lemma applied to $T=X_{p,\bullet}$, naturally in $p$, identifies it with the matching object in $q$, with boundary restriction as matching map. The relative matching map is therefore $\langle f/\delta_q\rangle$. The ground model of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] now gives the stated Joyal fibrations and rowwise Joyal weak equivalences. At degree zero the new lemma gives the terminal matching object and the component of $f$. Step 3 makes every initial map a cofibration, so every object is cofibrant. Functorial ground factorizations in the Kan and Joyal nodes yield functorial factorizations by the Reedy node's functorial-extension clause. All indices are small in the fixed universes.

source.place: Theorem 2.6 and Proposition 2.10, matching-map identification; functoriality from the existing Reedy theorem (Hovey Remark 5.2.3 and Theorem 5.2.5).

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is a vertical Reedy fibration, $a:U\hookrightarrow U'$ a monomorphism, and $b:V\to V'$ a Kan trivial cofibration. At horizontal degree $p$, the map $a\boxtimes' b$ is the coproduct of an identity on one copy of $V'$ for each $u\in U_p$ and a copy of $b$ for each $u\in U'_p\setminus U_p$: this follows by taking the degreewise pushout of sets and identifying $U_p$ with its image. This column map is a Kan trivial cofibration. Indeed, a square from that coproduct to any Kan fibration is a family of squares for $b$ and identities; fill the former by the Kan weak factorization system of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and the latter uniquely. The resulting family is the filler of the coproduct square, so the same weak factorization system identifies its left map as a trivial cofibration. Hence $a\boxtimes' b$ is a monomorphism and a columnwise weak equivalence, thus a vertical trivial cofibration by steps 3-4. The Reedy lifting axiom gives $(a\boxtimes' b)\pitchfork f$. Step 2 now gives $b\pitchfork\langle a\backslash f\rangle$ for every Kan trivial cofibration $b$, so $\langle a\backslash f\rangle$ is a Kan fibration. It also gives $a\pitchfork\langle f/b\rangle$ for every monomorphism $a$, which is the other asserted test. Conversely the all-monomorphism division test includes $a=\delta_p$, and hence gives the matching criterion. If instead only the last test is assumed, step 2 gives $b\pitchfork\langle\delta_p\backslash f\rangle$ for every Kan trivial cofibration $b$ and every $p$. The Kan weak factorization system makes these relative matching maps Kan fibrations, so $f$ is a vertical Reedy fibration. This proves both equivalences, without fibrancy assumptions on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 2.5; explicit coproduct-and-lifting proof of the all-monomorphism and all-anodyne criteria.

proof.text: Put $cL=*\boxtimes L$. For the mapping object in the item, operators are precomposition on $\Delta^q$. Composition sends maps $X\times c\Delta^q\to Y$ and $Y\times c\Delta^q\to Z$ to their composite using the same parameter in both places; the identity is the projection followed by $1_X$. Associativity and units hold pointwise. The tensor is $X\otimes L=X\times cL$, and the cotensor is specified by $(X^L)_{p,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(L\times\Delta^q,X_{p,\bullet})$, with operators by precomposition and the outer operators of $X$. The evaluation/currying formulas of step 1, with an extra factor $L$, identify maps $X\times cL\to Y$ with maps $L\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X,Y)$ and with maps $X\to Y^L$. For clarity, write $H=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X,Y)$ and define $(H^L)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(L\times\Delta^n,H)$. The ordinary currying bijection just proved, applied to $L\times\Delta^n$, identifies this set with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X\times cL\times c\Delta^n,Y)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X\otimes L,Y)_n$. Also $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X,Y^L)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X\times c\Delta^n,Y^L)$ is identified by the cotensor adjunction with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(X\times c\Delta^n\times cL,Y)$. Swapping the last two factors identifies this with the preceding set. These bijections commute with every $\Delta^m\to\Delta^n$ by precomposition, which proves both enriched adjunctions. These are actual functors by the commuting-operator definition of simplicial sets in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: Proposition 2.4 and the enrichment preceding it; degreewise tensor and cotensor formulas.

proof.text: Let $u:A\to B$ be a vertical Reedy cofibration and $b:L\to M$ a Kan cofibration. The tensor pushout product is $w:(B\times cL)\amalg_{A\times cL}(A\times cM)\to B\times cM$. It is a monomorphism in every bidegree, since its source is the union of the two indicated subsets of the product. Its column at $p$ is the ordinary simplicial pushout product of $u_p$ and $b$. If $u$ is vertically weak, each $u_p$ is a Kan trivial cofibration; if $b$ is weak, $b$ is a Kan trivial cofibration. A Kan trivial cofibration is exactly anodyne in the lifting-property sense of [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], because both mean left lifting against Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the weak factorization systems in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. That pushout-product node, using symmetry to interchange the factors when $u_p$ is trivial, therefore makes each column of $w$ a Kan trivial cofibration in either case. Thus $w$ is a vertical Reedy cofibration, trivial when $u$ or $b$ is weak. Transpose lifting squares using step 6. For a vertical Reedy fibration $f:X\to Y$, a square from $b$ to the relative simplicial mapping map for $(u,f)$ is exactly a square from $w$ to $f$, with the same filler. When $b$ is a Kan trivial cofibration, $w$ is vertically trivial, so such a filler exists. The relative mapping map is therefore a Kan fibration. If $u$ is weak, $w$ is vertically trivial for every Kan cofibration $b$; if $f$ is weak, $f$ lifts every vertical cofibration $w$. In either situation the relative mapping map lifts every monomorphism and is a Kan trivial fibration. This proves the simplicial-model lifting axiom, including its two triviality clauses. For the tensor unit, $X\otimes\Delta^0=X$ canonically, and $\Delta^0$ is Kan cofibrant because its initial map is a monomorphism. Taking its identity as cofibrant replacement verifies the unit condition directly. Together with step 6 this is the asserted simplicial vertical model structure.
